Independent bounded enumeration: all 28 cases with 2<=h<=5 and 1<=m<=7, at most 2^11 binary inputs per case, agreed. Replay by tallying the tuples of window ORs over all binary inputs, comparing all fiber sizes and the image/singleton criteria against the run classification, and extracting the two series coefficients by formal denominator division.
correctness.rationale: Each source one covers a clipped interval of output positions. For an interior one-run [a,b], the preceding and following output zeros force the first and last markers at a+h-1 and b, so L=b-a+1>=h is necessary. In between the markers the criterion is gaps at most h, giving the composition count c_h(L-h), including the coincident-marker case. A leading one-run of length a followed by a zero forces the source one at a; the preceding a-1 bits must avoid h zeros, and reversal handles the trailing run. Output-zero windows fix the other bits and separate the choices. An all-one output has exactly the source words with no h zeros and always at least two such words; all-zero has a single source. Therefore singleton outputs have boundary lengths 0 or 1 and interior lengths h or h+1, since compositions of d>=2 include both all ones and a part 2. For outputs with a zero the unambiguous grammar is E Z (I Z)* E, with Z=z/(1-z); use E=1/(1-z), I=z^h/(1-z) for reachability, E=1+z, I=z^h+z^(h+1) for uniqueness. Adding all-one outputs and the empty convention yields the claimed series. The source's shortcut from eventual coefficient positivity to a unique dominant pole is insufficient in isolation. Here the exact denominators suffice: at |z|<=rho_R, |1-z|>=1-|z|, with strict inequality at other points of |z|=rho_R, so (1-z)^2=z^(h+1) cannot vanish elsewhere in that disk. For U, equality in |z+z^(h+1)+z^(h+2)|<=rho_U+rho_U^(h+1)+rho_U^(h+2)=1 at a root forces z positive. Both positive roots are simple and give positive leading coefficients by the local simple-pole formula. The U denominator at rho_R is rho_R^2(1-rho_R)>0 and decreases strictly to its positive zero. Thus the claimed strict exponential ratio holds at every fixed h, with no width uniformity asserted.
residual_risks: The independent computation corroborates finitely many cases; the proof gives the all-width and all-length result. The coefficient asymptotic fixes h.

checked_sources: Assigned RESULT.md lines 4–23 and 30–51; Jen (1989) and cyclic Resultary 626495165f76 as comparison.
value.rationale: The exact enumerations distinguish two operationally different notions for a natural ordered sensor: a largest noiseless distinguishable codebook can select one representative per reachable output, but a singleton fiber decodes without imposing a codebook. The uniform-in-length formulas and strict fixed-width exponential gap explain why those two populations differ substantially; the full run-dependent list sizes make the result useful even when neither count alone suffices.
residual_risks: No conclusion for noise, circular or unordered data, constrained inputs, or a growing-width asymptotic.
